claims.statement: The CLI locates its configuration under $STEPPATH (default $HOME/.step, overridable with the STEPPATH environment variable); step.Init() from cli-utils runs before the CLI app starts.

step path prints the current authority path when a context is selected (or the base path otherwise), with --base for the base path and --profile for the current profile path, backed by step.Path(), step.BasePath(), and step.ProfilePath().

The STEPPATH layout includes certs/root_ca.crt for the bootstrap root and config/defaults.json containing ca-url, fingerprint, and root plus optional redirect-url, provisioner, and min-password-length fields written by the bootstrap flow.
contexts.json maps each context name to an object with authority and profile, and current-context.json holds {"context": "<name>"} selecting the default context.
Each context owns an authorities/<authority>/ directory and a profiles/<profile>/ directory under the base path, as shown by step path examples.
The plugin loader looks for step-<name>-plugin binaries under $STEPPATH/plugins with platform extensions on Windows.
Removing a context also removes the matching authority line from $(step path --base)/ssh/includes.
The step context command group ("manage certificate authority contexts") registers the current, list, remove, and select subcommands.
step context list prints all context names alphabetically with the current one prefixed by a play marker.
step context current prints the current context name, or a {name, authority, profile} JSON object with --json, and errors "no context selected" when none is set.
step context select <name> sets the default context via step.Contexts().SaveCurrent(name).

step context remove <name> removes the authority directory only if no other context shares that authority and the profile directory only if unshared, prompting for confirmation unless --force is passed, and refuses to remove the current context.

HiddenNoContext is a hidden --no-context BoolT flag meaning "do not apply context specific environment for this command", declared by all step context subcommands so they are not affected by the context environment they manage.
cautils.UseContext returns true when step contexts are enabled or any of the --context, --authority, or --profile flags is set.
step ca init creates a context (name defaulting to the first DNS name, authority and profile defaulting to the name), then saves it as current and sets it via step.Contexts().

bootstrap() downloads the root via client.Root(fingerprint), writes it to the root CA path with mode 0600, writes defaults.json from bootstrapConfig, injects the resolved ca-url/fingerprint/root into the current cli.Context, and installs the root into the system truststore with --install.

BootstrapTeamAuthority queries https://api.smallstep.com/v1/teams/<team>/authorities/<authority> (or a --team-url with <> replaced by the team ID), decodes a bootstrapAPIResponse with url, fingerprint, redirect-url, provisioner, and min-password-length, and bootstraps with the default context name <team-authority>.<team>.
BootstrapAuthority bootstraps an authority from just a CA URL and fingerprint, using the CA host (or --authority) as the default context name.
WarnContext prints a notice suggesting contexts when step is already configured with a config/ca.json but contexts are not in use.

Flag resolution to a context: explicit flags win (ParseCaURL only requires --ca-url when --offline is not set), defaults.json stores ca-url/fingerprint/root so commands do not need to repeat them after bootstrap, and flags.Identity exists so the identity can be configured in $STEPPATH/config/defaults.json.

The merge of the current context's defaults and profile into flag values is implemented in github.com/smallstep/cli-utils (step.Init, step.Contexts, step.Path, step.BasePath, step.DefaultsFile, step.ProfileDefaultsFile), which is outside this repo, so the exact precedence rules are not verifiable from this codebase; this repo only references those entry points.

CA connection shared flags are CaURL (--ca-url), Root (--root), Context (--context), ContextProfile (--profile), ContextAuthority (--authority), Offline (--offline), and CaConfig (--ca-config, default $(step path)/config/ca.json).

Provisioner and admin auth shared flags include Provisioner (provisioner,issuer), AdminProvisioner, AdminSubject, AdminPasswordFile (aliased password-file), AdminPasswordFileNoAlias, ProvisionerPasswordFile, ProvisionerPasswordFileWithAlias, AdminCert, and AdminKey.
Token header shared flags include X5cCert/X5cKey/X5cChain/X5cInsecure, X5tCert/X5tKey, SSHPOPCert/SSHPOPKey, and NebulaCert/NebulaKey for JWT/JWS header certificates and signing keys.

Confirmation (cnf) and ConfirmationFile (cnf-file) restrict a token to a CSR fingerprint or CSR file, and K8sSATokenPathFlag (default /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token) configures the Kubernetes service account token path.

Key material shared flags are KTY (kty, default EC for EC/OKP/RSA), Size (size, bits for RSA and oct keys), Curve (crv,curve, default P-256 for EC and Ed25519 for OKP), and Subtle/SubtleHidden for delicate operations.
Time-bound shared flags are NotBefore/NotAfter and the SSH-only CertNotBefore/CertNotAfter, each accepting RFC 3339 time or a duration, parsed by ParseTimeOrDuration and ParseTimeDuration.
Behavior shared flags include Force, DryRun, Insecure/InsecureHidden, NoPassword (documented to require --insecure) and PasswordFile, Token, NoPager, Limit, Console, and Comment.

Template shared flags are Template (certificate template JSON file), TemplateSet (repeated --set key=value), and TemplateSetFile (JSON file), merged by GetTemplateData where --set values are used raw when not valid JSON, and serialized by ParseTemplateData.

Team and OAuth shared flags include Team, TeamURL (with <> placeholders replaced by the team ID), TeamAuthority, RedirectURL, ServerName (TLS SNI), Identity, EABKeyID, EABReference, KMSUri (KMS/HSM URI), and AttestationURI.

FingerprintFormatFlag produces a --format flag (hex, base64, base64-url, base64-url-raw, base64-raw, or emoji) and FingerprintCertificateModeFlag produces --certificate to include SSH certificate bytes in the fingerprint; ParseFingerprintFormat maps the strings to fingerprint encodings.

ParseCaURL/ParseCaURLIfExists/parseCaURL require a non-empty CA URL unless offline, prepend https:// when no scheme is given, reject non-https schemes, and normalize bracket-less IPv6 hosts (including extracting an appended port).
FirstStringOf returns the value of the first explicitly set flag from a list of aliased flags, or the first non-empty default value when none is set.
The app defines a global --config flag ("path to the config file to use for CLI flags"); its consumption happens in the cli-utils startup path rather than in this repo.

internal/command/inject.go provides InjectContext, which prepends a middleware pinning a pre-built context.Context so later middlewares operate on it, and wrap, which runs the middleware chain over a fresh context.Background() and attaches the cli.Context under a private key; CLIContextFromContext recovers the cli.Context and panics when absent.
Commands that must build their context before the action runs, such as the step ca policy actions, use command.InjectContext as their cli Action.
When no root is supplied, token claims default to the root certificate in the $STEPPATH secrets directory (WithRootCA calculates the SHA256 for token claims).

Adding a shared flag means adding it to the var block in flags/flags.go with a documented Usage using the <placeholder> convention (help stringifies the first <...>), adding a Parse* helper next to existing ones when parsing is needed, wiring it into command Flags lists, and keeping hidden variants for flags that must be accepted but not shown.

Adding a context-aware behavior means gating on cautils.UseContext, reading or writing contexts only through step.Contexts() (Add/Get/GetCurrent/SaveCurrent/SetCurrent/Remove) with values stored in the authority/profile directories, and adding flags.HiddenNoContext to commands that should not receive the context environment.
